title: Cubs' Swanson sidelined 4-6 weeks with Grade 2 oblique strain
dek: Chicago Cubs shortstop Dansby Swanson has a Grade 2 oblique strain and is expected to miss four to six weeks, according to sources cited by ESPN. The timeline could eliminate him from the remainder of the regular season as the Cubs chase the NL Central and defend their wild-card position.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Cubs shortstop Dansby Swanson has a Grade 2 oblique strain and is expected to miss four to six weeks, per ESPN sources.
bottom_line: Watch for official Cubs confirmation of the injury status and any revision to the recovery timeline as medical evaluations continue. The critical date is late September, when the four to six-week window expires and determines whether Swanson can return for a playoff push.
body: Chicago Cubs shortstop Dansby Swanson has a Grade 2 oblique strain and is expected to miss four to six weeks, according to sources cited by ESPN. The injury timeline could eliminate him from the remainder of the regular season as the Cubs fight for playoff positioning in the final weeks.

Swanson left Sunday's 11-4 loss to the St. Louis Cardinals after exiting in the bottom of the third inning due to left side discomfort following an awkward swing-and-miss, per ESPN. Manager Craig Counsell said Swanson would be placed on the injured list after the game.

Before the injury, Swanson was hitting .216 with 18 home runs and 66 RBIs while batting lower in the lineup. The two-time Gold Glove winner (2022, 2023) is an annual contender for the award and represents one of the league's elite defensive shortstops.

The Cubs, who sit at 72-53, trail the Milwaukee Brewers by five games in the National League Central and hold a firm grip on the top NL wild-card spot, per ESPN. A four to six-week absence would extend well into late September and potentially through the playoff chase.

Nico Hoerner moved from second base to shortstop following Swanson's injury and will likely continue there, according to ESPN. Rookie Pedro Ramirez is expected to man second base in Swanson's absence, giving the Cubs an infield with two rookies or shifted players in critical defensive positions during a pennant race.

The Grade 2 classification and four to six-week timeline come from unnamed sources cited by ESPN's Jesse Rogers. No official statement from the Cubs organization or medical staff independently confirming the designation or recovery window appears in the available reporting. The exact extent of imaging, if any, used to confirm the Grade 2 status is not disclosed in the source material.
